posts.why: Closing the month by being the client is the cleanest ending.

slides: Before: helping brands tell their story

The advice we spent a month giving, applied to ourselves, in public.

posts.topic: Nobody is on social to be sold to
posts.why: The governing sentence of the whole month, and its evidence.

tiktok.hook: Nobody is on social to be sold to. So we entertained first.
tiktok.vo: Nobody is on social to be sold to, so we entertained first, taught the ones who were interested, and made it as easy as possible for the ones who had already decided. Sixty, thirty, ten. What happened was not a viral month. What happened was that the sell posts did not feel like a betrayal, because they arrived after three weeks of being useful and nobody had to be tricked into watching them.
tiktok.cap: Entertain everyone, teach the interested, make it easy for the decided. 60/30/10.
tiktok.body: Entertained first, taught the interested, made it easy for the decided. Sixty, thirty, ten. No viral month; the sell posts simply did not feel like a betrayal.

slides: Nobody wants to be sold to
instagram.cap:
This is the one idea worth carrying into December, and it does not require posting more. It requires posting in this order.

The sell posts worked because of the twenty-seven days before them.

facebook.body:
Nobody is on social to be sold to.

So we entertained first, taught the ones who were interested, and made it as easy as possible for the ones who had already decided. Sixty percent, thirty, ten.

What happened was not a viral month. What happened was that the sell posts did not feel like a betrayal, because they arrived after three weeks of being useful.

Nobody had to be tricked into watching them.

posts.topic: The whole system in one post
posts.why: The month's deliverable, compressed to something copyable.

tiktok.hook: The whole system in one post: entertain, teach, sell. Sixty, thirty, ten.
tiktok.vo: The whole system, in one post. Eleven slots a day. Seven entertain, three teach, one sell. Four repeating formats so you are not inventing from nothing every morning. One spreadsheet with a date and a time for each slot. Read it on the last day of the month, keep what worked, throw out the rest, and do it again. That is the entire system and it fits in a caption.
tiktok.cap: 11 slots · 7 entertain · 3 teach · 1 sell · 4 formats · 1 sheet · 30 days.
tiktok.body: Eleven slots, seven entertain, three teach, one sell. Four repeating formats. One sheet with dates and times. Read it on the last day, keep what worked, repeat.

instagram.cap:
Most content plans fail because they are too elaborate to repeat on a bad week. This one is deliberately small.

A system you can describe in one caption is a system you will actually run.

facebook.body:
The whole system, in one post.

11 slots a day. Seven entertain, three teach, one sell. Four repeating formats, so you are not inventing from nothing every morning. One spreadsheet with a date and a time for each slot.

Read it on the last day of the month. Keep what worked. Throw out the rest. Do it again.

That is the entire system, and it fits in a caption.

posts.topic: Posting less would have been the bigger risk
posts.why: Answers the obvious objection to the whole month's method.

tiktok.hook: Posting less would have been the bigger risk. Here is why.
tiktok.vo: Posting less would have been the bigger risk, and I know that is the opposite of what most advice says. Fewer posts means fewer attempts, which means fewer discoveries, and you would still spend the same six weeks finding out. Volume is not a virtue. It is a search method, and searching is the only way to find the twenty percent that carries everything.
tiktok.cap: Volume is not a virtue. It is a search method.
tiktok.body: Fewer posts means fewer attempts and fewer discoveries, and you would still spend the same six weeks finding out. Volume is a search method, not a virtue.

instagram.cap:
The honest version of the volume argument is not that more is better. It is that more is faster to learn from, and only if you read the sheet.

You can post less and learn less at the same speed.

facebook.body:
Posting less would have been the bigger risk — the opposite of what most advice says.

Fewer posts means fewer attempts, which means fewer discoveries. You would still spend the same six weeks finding out.

Volume is not a virtue. It is a search method, and searching is the only way to find the twenty percent that carries everything.

What have you found by volume?

posts.why: Refusing the big claim at the end is the strongest possible credibility move.

tiktok.hook: What this month actually changed, and only what is true.
beats: And we know what to cut
tiktok.vo: What this month actually changed, and only what is true. No viral moment. A handful of conversations. One habit changed, which is answering faster. And we now know, from four weeks of evidence rather than a hunch, which three formats to cut and which one to double. That is a smaller result than a launch video would promise and it is the one I can defend in a room with the sheet in front of me.
tiktok.cap: No viral moment. Some conversations. One habit changed. Three formats to cut.
tiktok.body: One habit changed, which is answering faster. And four weeks of evidence on which three formats to cut. Smaller than a launch video would promise, and defensible with the sheet open.

instagram.cap:
Anyone can report a feeling. Reporting the numbers that are smaller than expected is what makes the numbers that are larger than expected believable.

A result you can defend with the sheet open is the only result worth reporting.

facebook.body:
What this month actually changed, and only what is true.

No viral moment. A handful of conversations. One habit changed, which is answering faster. And we now know, from four weeks of evidence rather than a hunch, which three formats to cut and which one to double.

A smaller result than a launch video would promise — and the only one I can defend with the sheet open.

posts.why: Showing the actual instrument is what separates this from advice.

tiktok.hook: Here is the tracker, on camera, with the real columns.
tiktok.vo: Here is the tracker, on camera, with the real columns: date, day, format, type, views, saves, comments, conversations, and packs sold. Nine columns, one row per post, filled in every morning by hand. The only column that ever made me change what I post is conversations, and the only one that ever surprised me is saves, because saves and views have almost nothing to do with each other.
tiktok.cap: Nine columns, one row a post, filled by hand. Conversations changed the plan. Saves surprised me.
tiktok.body: Date, format, type, views, saves, comments, conversations, sales. Nine columns, filled by hand every morning. Conversations changed the plan; saves surprised me.

instagram.cap:
A spreadsheet you fill in by hand forces you to look at every post, which is the actual benefit. The data is almost secondary.

Nine columns beat any dashboard with forty.

facebook.body:
The tracker, on camera, with the real columns:

date · format · type · views · saves · comments · conversations · packs sold

Nine columns. One row per post. Filled in by hand every morning.

The only column that ever changed what I post is conversations. The only one that surprised me is saves — saves and views have almost nothing to do with each other.

Would you fill this in?

posts.topic: The one post I would keep
posts.why: A single answer is more memorable than a list of favourites.

tiktok.hook: One post from this month worth keeping: the day-three message.
tiktok.vo: If we could keep one post from the whole month, it would be the day three message, word for word. Not the best performing one, not the funniest one. That one, because it is the only thing we published that somebody can copy in ten seconds and use before lunch, and the whole account exists to produce things like that. Everything else was practice.
tiktok.cap: One message, copyable in ten seconds, used before lunch. That is the whole point.
tiktok.body: Not the best performer, not the funniest. The one somebody can copy in ten seconds and use before lunch. Everything else was practice.

instagram.cap:
This is the test I would apply to any account, including mine: did anything you published get used by somebody within a day?

Judge posts by what someone can use before lunch.

facebook.body:
If we could keep one post from the whole month, it would be the day-three message, word for word.

Not the best performing. Not the funniest.

That one, because it is the only thing we published that somebody can copy in ten seconds and use before lunch.

The whole account exists to produce things like that. Everything else was practice.

posts.topic: What do you want next month
posts.why: Ending by asking is the cleanest possible handover.

tiktok.hook: I asked what they want next month, then committed on camera.
tiktok.vo: I asked people what they wanted next month. More teardowns came first, more real prices second, and one person asked for more of the chat scripts, which surprised me because they are the least visual thing we make. So here is the commitment, on camera: one teardown a day in December, every day, real businesses, three fixes each. If I do not do it, come back on the thirty first and say so.
tiktok.cap: Committed on camera: one teardown a day in December. Hold me to it.
tiktok.body: More teardowns, more real prices, more chat scripts. So the commitment, on camera: one teardown a day in December, real businesses, three fixes each.

instagram.cap:
Committing to one thing publicly is worth more than a roadmap of nine, because one can be checked.

Ask, then commit to one thing. Not three.

facebook.body:
I asked people what they wanted next month.

More teardowns came first. More real prices second. One person asked for more chat scripts, which surprised me because they are the least visual thing we make.

So here is the commitment, on camera: one teardown a day in December. Real businesses. Three fixes each.

If I do not do it, come back on the 31st and say so.

posts.topic: The version of this that was easier
posts.why: Naming the temptation is the most honest possible ending.

tiktok.hook: The thing we refused this month was the easier version of this.
tiktok.vo: The thing we refused this month was the easier version of this account: bigger claims, a wall of invented results, countdowns that reset every Friday, and a course at the end of it. That version would probably have grown faster. It would also have been a thing I had to maintain, and I would rather spend the next year writing about quotes than defending a number I made up in November.
tiktok.cap: The easier version would have grown faster. It would also have to be maintained.
tiktok.body: Bigger claims, invented results, countdowns that reset, a course at the end. It would probably have grown faster, and it would have to be maintained forever.

instagram.cap:
This is the last refusal of the month and it is the one that explains all the others. Everything we turned down was some version of that same trade.

A lie needs maintenance. A limit does not.

facebook.body:
The thing we refused this month was the easier version of this account.

Bigger claims. A wall of invented results. Countdowns that reset every Friday. A course at the end of it.

That version would probably have grown faster.

It would also have been something I had to maintain — and I would rather spend next year writing about quotes than defending a number I made up in November.
